name: Mikhail Bakunin
description: Anarchist theorist assessed through voluntary federation and collective ownership, with discriminatory writings included as counter-evidence.

axes.brief: Rejected state domination and representative elites; favoured freely organised associations, direct participation and recallable delegates.
axes.counter: Even competitive national elections reproduce state authority in his ideal; responses on national institutions are conditional comparisons, not endorsement of a permanent national government.

axes.brief: Opposed coercive state authority, censorship and police domination in favour of personal and associational freedom.
axes.counter: Revolutionary force and concealed organisational coordination qualify ideal liberty; security conditions in modern warrant questions require cautious analogy.

axes.brief: Free federation and ethnic autonomy opposed state-enforced homogenisation.
axes.counter: His 1871 antisemitic collective stereotypes contradict an unqualified multicultural image. Earlier pan-Slavic context is not mechanically imported into every mature-policy answer.

axes.brief: Free association and solidarity imply freer movement and family settlement than coercive state borders.
axes.counter: His discriminatory rhetoric weakens confidence in universally equal treatment; modern public benefits presuppose a state he sought to abolish and are qualified analogies.

axes.brief: Opposed imperial states and militarism but endorsed armed revolutionary self-defence and resistance.
axes.counter: Revolutionary violence is not pacifism; a standing national expeditionary army and sovereign war-for-advantage were not his ideal.

axes.brief: Favoured cross-border federation of voluntary worker and local associations rather than sovereign nation-state supremacy.
axes.counter: International bureaucracy compelling free associations would reproduce domination; weak agreement with common institutions means voluntary federation, not unconditional international state rule.

axes.brief: Collective worker ownership and common productive resources should replace capitalists’ private control.
axes.counter: He rejected government ownership and state socialism; Neutral on several public-body questions expresses the substantive difference between voluntary collective ownership and national state ownership, not missing evidence.

axes.brief: Opposed coercive economic barriers between freely associated producers and communities.
axes.counter: Freedom of exchange is not acceptance of capitalist dominance, strategic corporate concentration or unequal ownership; anti-state terms need careful translation.

axes.brief: Decentralised cooperative production and negotiated association should replace compulsory state plans.
axes.counter: A collective social economy is not conventional capitalist market allocation; worker coordination may plan voluntarily, while national production targets and state-directed banking are rejected.

axes.brief: Abolition of concentrated inherited wealth and collective economic equality were priorities.
axes.counter: State taxation and benefits are not his preferred mechanism. Neutral on tax-and-benefit equalisation expresses support for the aim with rejection of the coercive state means; progressive ownership reform is not merely low redistribution.

axes.brief: Rejected theological and clerical authority over law, schools and public institutions.
axes.counter: Religious belief could remain voluntary; anti-clerical argument is not permission to suppress private believers. His antisemitism must be separately disclosed rather than excused as secularism.

axes.brief: Favoured freedom of unions and emancipation from inherited social and religious hierarchy.
axes.counter: The mature writings do not establish every modern LGBT or reproductive-policy response; broad egalitarian aims are qualified estimates and do not negate discriminatory counter-evidence.

axes.brief: Science and human development were valued without rule by scientific elites.
axes.counter: Criticism of scientific government and all coercive authority qualifies enthusiasm; modern enhancement and ecological risks have no direct textual counterparts.

axes.brief: Bottom-up free federation of communes and regions should preserve association and exit.
axes.counter: Nationally uniform employment and healthcare goals cannot automatically justify coercive central administration; voluntary coordination during disasters differs from imposed command.

axes.brief: Social institutions and education shape human possibilities, alongside physical and inherited conditions acknowledged in materialism.
axes.counter: His antisemitic generalisations attributed collective character to a people and weaken purely social explanations. Race-specific violence and IQ propositions remain uncertain; no endorsement is fabricated from stereotypes alone.
